testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, what should you do?

options.text: Put the vehicle in low gear and use engine braking.
Keep downshifting instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in low gear and use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On long or steep hills, use engine braking to control your speed. Use the regular brakes only as a backup.

questions.question: What color light shows when the ABS is not working?
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns you when the ABS is not working. Know where this light is on your vehicle before you drive.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, what can a separate air tank do?

options.text: Make the air brakes work better.
Fill the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.explanation: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time if low air pressure has activated them. This allows you to move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: When do the rods in S-cam brakes move the slack adjusters?

options.text: When the driver presses the brake pedal.
When the driver uses the emergency brake.
When the driver uses the trailer hand valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the driver presses the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. This air pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage for a triple combination vehicle in one minute?
questions.explanation: For a triple combination vehicle, the air leakage rate should not be higher than 6 psi in one minute.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: They are not allowed on vehicles.
They hold compressed air for the brakes.
They should be emptied after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: They hold compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold the compressed air used by the braking system. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of tanks.

questions.question: What shows how much air pressure is in your vehicle's air tanks?
questions.explanation: The supply pressure gauge tells you how much air pressure is in your vehicle's air tanks.

questions.question: What do wheel chocks do on flat surfaces?

options.text: They stop a parked vehicle from moving.
They make a parked vehicle roll easier.
They should only be used on the front driver's side tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: They stop a parked vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: When you cannot use a parking brake, wheel chocks can hold a parked vehicle in place on a level surface.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, what should turn on when air pressure drops below 45 psi?
questions.explanation: Spring brakes should turn on automatically when air tank pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. Test this by chocking the wheels and using the brake pedal to release air from the system. The parking brake valve should pop out and spring brakes should engage when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: They should not be used in cold weather.
They remove water and oil from the air tanks.
They send air to the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and oil that can damage the brake system. Air tanks have drain valves to remove this water and oil.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?

options.text: The brakes may be slow to respond.

questions.explanation: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too often lets air out of the brake system faster than the compressor can refill it. If pressure gets too low, the air brakes may stop working.

questions.question: When air tanks reach 125 psi, the air compressor governor will:

options.text: Stop the compressor from pumping air.
Start pumping air into the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping air when tanks reach about 125 psi. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: During an emergency stop, you should:

options.text: Swerve your trailer to the right and stop.
Swerve your trailer to the left and stop.

questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, use controlled braking or stab braking. Keep your vehicle in a straight line while braking, but stay ready to turn if needed.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: the service brake, the parking brake, and the emergency brake. The emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: Friction in an S-cam brake happens when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Press against the outside of the brake drum.
Press against the inside of the brake drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction occurs when brake shoes and linings press against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: When parked on a flat surface, you should:

options.text: Use wheel chocks to keep your vehicle from moving.
Use wheel chocks only if you have applied the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to keep your vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: Always use wheel chocks when parking on a flat surface. If the vehicle does not have spring brakes, wheel chocks are essential to prevent the trailer from moving.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Reduce a vehicle's normal braking power.
Work in addition to other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
Are not effective on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work in addition to other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works with your vehicle's normal braking system and does not increase or decrease braking power. ABS only activates when the vehicle's wheels are about to lock.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brake system parts include: air compressor, governor, air storage tanks, tank drains, alcohol evaporator, safety valve, brake pedal, foundation brakes, supply and application gauges, low air pressure warning signal, stop light switch, spring brakes, and parking brake controls.

questions.question: A ____ allows a driver to slowly apply spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes. On equipped vehicles, a lever on the dashboard controls this valve.

questions.question: An air compressor governor controls:

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
The temperature of the air pumped into the air storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.

questions.question: When spring brakes are on, you should never:
questions.explanation: Do not push the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. The combined force from the springs and air pressure can damage the brakes.

questions.question: For a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should not exceed ____ psi in one minute during a static leakage test.
questions.explanation: The leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle with air brakes should not exceed 5 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, do not drive the vehicle. Something needs to be fixed.

questions.question: A wig wag is:

options.text: A tube that carries air to the brakes.
A type of air brake system.

questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device required on vehicles with air brakes. It drops a mechanical arm into your view when air pressure in the tanks drops to between 55 and 75 psi.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, if one air system is very low on pressure:

options.text: None of the brakes will work.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There is usually no noticeable effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully if one air system loses pressure. If this happens while driving, exit the road and park as soon as possible.

questions.question: What is often found in compressed air?
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Tanks must be drained regularly to remove this buildup.
